# 1 Enoch Chapter 37 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 37:2 — "dry ground" vs. "earth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those who-dwell upon the-dry-ground" | Preserves Ge'ez yābaśt (dry land, as opposed to sea) |
| LOGOS | "those who dwell upon the dry ground" | Retains the specificity of the Ge'ez term |
| PNEUMA | "all who inhabit the earth" | Natural English; "dry ground" sounds archaic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "dry ground" (EMET/LOGOS). The Ge'ez yābaśt is a deliberate term contrasting habitable land with the waters. PNEUMA's "earth" loses this nuance. Minor archaic flavor is acceptable given the genre.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 37:2 — "Hear, O men of former times" vs. "Listen, all you people of ancient times"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Hear, ye men of-old-time" | Literal; preserves imperative + archaic plural |
| LOGOS | "Hear, O men of former times" | Formal; modernizes "ye" while keeping the address form |
| PNEUMA | "Listen, all you people of ancient times" | Adds "all" for emphasis; natural contemporary English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Hear, O men of former times" (LOGOS). "Hear" is the traditional prophetic call and should be preserved. PNEUMA's added "all" has no Ge'ez basis.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 37:4 — "good pleasure" vs. "will"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "good-pleasure of-the-Lord of-Spirits" | Literal; Ge'ez fəqr implies delight/desire |
| LOGOS | "good pleasure of the Lord of Spirits" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "will of the Lord of Spirits" | Simplified; "good pleasure" sounds old-fashioned |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "good pleasure" (EMET/LOGOS). The term carries the sense of divine delight in Enoch's mission, not merely volitional decision. This nuance matters theologically.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 37:4 — "portion of eternal life" vs. "share in eternal life"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lot of eternal-life" | Literal; Ge'ez ḥelq = portion/lot |
| LOGOS | "portion of eternal life" | Formal; "portion" more natural than "lot" |
| PNEUMA | "share in eternal life" | Idiomatic English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "portion of eternal life" (LOGOS). "Lot" (EMET) is accurate but feels like a lottery term in English. "Share" (PNEUMA) is vaguer. "Portion" best conveys the sense of an allotted share.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements: 4**
